citation.title: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series
citation.authors: Patrick Kidger, James Morrill, James Foster, Terry Lyons
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS 2020)

topic: Continuous-time sequence model (Neural CDE) for irregularly sampled, partially observed time series; machine-learning benchmarks, not plasma.
own_question: How can a Neural ODE incorporate data that arrives after the initial condition? The authors propose driving the hidden state with an interpolated data path.
actual_method_and_evidence: Natural cubic spline interpolation of the data, with time added as a channel, forms the driving path X. Training uses adjoint backpropagation. The paper includes universal-approximation and subsumption proofs (Appendices B and C). Classification experiments use CharacterTrajectories, PhysioNet sepsis and Speech Commands, comparing against GRU and ODE-RNN baselines over 5 runs with random 70/15/15 splits. The authors state in Sec. 6.4 that cubic splines are non-causal, so the reported setup cannot run in real time.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Continuous-time models for irregular sampling exist. In Neural CDEs, the hidden state is driven by an interpolated observation path.
claim_checks.qualification: The authors themselves say spline-based X uses future observations (non-causal). This is ML classification work, not nowcasting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The interpolation path at time t depends on later samples. The paper has no arrival-time or online evaluation.
validation_if_relevant: Random splits on non-plasma datasets. There is no held-out campaign analogue.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim Neural CDEs are causal or suitable for real-time use as published.
Do not transfer the reported accuracy or memory results to CES/BES/ECEI.
Do not imply we implemented a Neural CDE.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background on irregular-sampling ML models. Its non-causal interpolation contrasts with our strictly-past inputs. It is not needed for the core framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
